28278.description:
10 roles. 3 provinces. 1 mission: climate-resilient farming for PNG.
From provincial coordination to national leadership — pick your role.
Real impact, real careers — help PNG farmers adapt and thrive.
About the Organisation and the Project
The South Pacific Community (SPC) — the region's principal intergovernmental organisation, working across the Pacific since 1947 — and the Global Green Growth Institute (GGGI), a treaty-based international body supporting sustainable development, have partnered with Papua New Guinea's Department of Agriculture and Livestock (DAL) to deliver the Agriculture Sector Support Activity (ASSA).
Formally known as the Adaptation of Small-Scale Agriculture for Improved Food Security of Resilient Communities in Papua New Guinea, ASSA is a landmark, multi-year initiative that will work directly with farming communities across Enga, Milne Bay and New Ireland Provinces. Its purpose is to strengthen food security, build climate-resilient agricultural practices and help communities better anticipate, prepare for and respond to climate variability and climate-related shocks — with DAL acting as the Implementing Agency and SPC and GGGI providing funding and technical backing.
About This Recruitment
To build the team that will lead this work, ASSA has partnered with Peopleconnexion to manage end-to-end recruitment for its Project Management Unit (PMU) — a ten-person team responsible for delivering the project on the ground. These roles give you the opportunity to contribute to regional or national impact, and the chance to be part of a program that will shape climate adaptation practice in PNG agriculture for years to come.
If you want a career that puts you at the centre of one of PNG's most significant climate adaptation investments, Peopleconnexion wants to hear from you.
About the Role
How do we know ASSA is working? That's your job. As MEL Manager, you will design and lead the project's monitoring, evaluation, learning and reporting systems and Results Framework — turning field data into evidence that drives smarter decisions, stronger reporting and real proof of impact for communities, DAL, SPC and the Adaptation Fund.
Key Responsibilities
Establish and lead the project's MEL systems and Results Framework implementation.
Measure and report on project performance, outcomes and impact.
Use evidence and data to inform adaptive management and improve delivery.
Develop and manage performance indicators, reporting frameworks and evaluation processes.
Produce high-quality reports for the PMU, DAL, SPC and donor stakeholders.
Champion organisational learning and the capture of lessons learned and good practice.
What You'll Bring
A bachelor's degree in M&E, economics, statistics, development studies, project management, agriculture, environmental management, social sciences or related field.
Demonstrated experience designing and implementing M&E systems and using data to improve outcomes.
A track record producing credible, high-quality reporting for management, donors or governance bodies.
Strong analytical thinking and a genuine interest in evidence-based development practice.
Why Join the ASSA Team?
Be part of a landmark, multi-year climate adaptation program with real, visible impact for PNG farming communities.
Competitive remuneration aligned to PNG Public Service General Orders (and SPC salary bands for specialist roles).
Work alongside a capable, mission-driven, multidisciplinary team backed by SPC, GGGI and DAL.
A fixed-term contract for the duration of the project (up to five years), subject to performance and funding.
How to Apply
Applications close COB Monday 07th September 2026.
Please submit your CV and a cover letter addressing the selection criteria by clicking on the ‘APPLY NOW’ button
While the strong preference is to build a PNG-led team, for select specialist roles applications are also welcomed from suitably qualified international candidates.
Ten roles. Three provinces. One opportunity to help shape the future of climate-resilient agriculture in Papua New Guinea.
Apply

About the Organisation and the Project
The South Pacific Community (SPC) — the region's principal intergovernmental organisation, working across the Pacific since 1947 — and the Global Green Growth Institute (GGGI), a treaty-based international body supporting sustainable development, have partnered with Papua New Guinea's Department of Agriculture and Livestock (DAL) to deliver the Agriculture Sector Support Activity (ASSA).
Formally known as the Adaptation of Small-Scale Agriculture for Improved Food Security of Resilient Communities in Papua New Guinea, ASSA is a landmark, multi-year initiative that will work directly with farming communities across Enga, Milne Bay and New Ireland Provinces. Its purpose is to strengthen food security, build climate-resilient agricultural practices and help communities better anticipate, prepare for and respond to climate variability and climate-related shocks — with DAL acting as the Implementing Agency and SPC and GGGI providing funding and technical backing.
About This Recruitment
To build the team that will lead this work, ASSA has partnered with Peopleconnexion to manage end-to-end recruitment for its Project Management Unit (PMU) — a ten-person team responsible for delivering the project on the ground. These roles give you the opportunity to contribute to regional or national impact, and the chance to be part of a program that will shape climate adaptation practice in PNG agriculture for years to come.
If you want a career that puts you at the centre of one of PNG's most significant climate adaptation investments, Peopleconnexion wants to hear from you.
About the Role
From coastal erosion to saltwater intrusion, Milne Bay’s Island and coastal communities face some of PNG's toughest climate pressures. As Provincial Project Coordinator, you'll be the driving force behind ASSA's presence in Milne Bay — coordinating activities across a dispersed and diverse province, connecting communities to resources and support, and helping farming and fishing households build lasting resilience.
Key Responsibilities
Coordinate day-to-day project implementation across Milne Bay's coastal and island communities.
Build strong relationships with provincial and district administrations, LLGs, community leaders and farmer groups.

A bachelor's degree in agriculture, environmental management, climate change, development studies, project management, natural resource management or related field.

Comfort operating in remote, island and logistically complex environments.

28268.description:
Ok Tedi Development Foundation (OTDF)
is a not-for-profit organization, operating independently of Ok Tedi Mining Limited since 2010, and is a 100% owned Papua New Guinea company mandated to ensure the wise and sustainable use of the wealth created from mining operations for future generations and delivers projects to communities through a unique partnership between mining, the people and government of Papua New Guinea.
Applications are now open for qualified and experienced professionals to join the executive management team, based in Kiunga, Western Province.
EXECUTIVE MANAGER – CORPORATE SERVICES
This role reports to the Chief Executive Officer and is a member of the Executive Management Team. The EM-CS provides leadership and direction to achieve agreed strategies, objectives and annual targets for the corporate services functions (including Finance, Human Resources, Occupational Health & Safety, Information Services, CMCA Trust Administration and Media & Communications), guided by the OTDF Strategic Direction, annual workplans, budgets, policies and procedures approved by the Board of Directors.
Key Responsibilities
Ensure all OTDF financial, performance, audit, and statutory reporting obligations are met accurately and within required timeframes, including reporting to CEO, the Board, funding organizations, OTDF project leaders, and other stakeholders, utilizing established Monitoring and Evaluation frameworks.
Lead and manage all internal and external financial audit processes, including coordination with external auditors, timely resolution of audit findings, implementation of agreed recommendations, and reporting of audit outcomes to the Chief Executive Officer and Board.
Maintain executive accountability for the development, implementation, and continuous review of OTDF corporate service policies, systems, and procedures, ensuring they remain current, fit-for-purpose, and fully complied with by staff and contractors.
Chair relevant OTDF Committees, including the Tender Committee, ensuring committee deliberations are underpinned by strong probity, transparency, and value-for-money principles.
Represent OTDF in internal and external forums as delegated by the Chief Executive Officer, including participation in annual Communications Patrols and other stakeholder engagement activities.
Provide strategic leadership to staff to deliver the objectives and performance targets outlined in the OTDF Strategic Direction 2021–2025 (and successor plans), with responsibility for financial management, audit, and corporate services outcomes
Ensure all statutory and operational insurance policies are proactively reviewed, maintained, and renewed within required timeframes to adequately manage organizational risk.
Lead research, analysis, and implementation of continuous business improvement initiatives across management accounting, financial systems, audit readiness, and broader corporate service functions to enhance organizational efficiency, effectiveness, and accountability.
Ensure OTDF’s occupational health and safety programs and systems are strategically planned, implemented, monitored, and adequately resourced to achieve a zero-harm culture for employees and contractors.
Champion a strong corporate culture grounded in ethical conduct, integrity, and accountability, fostering a positive and professional workplace environment that attracts, develops, and retains high-performing staff.
Proactively advise the Chief Executive Officer on emerging financial, audit, governance, compliance, or operational risks within areas of responsibility, and provide clear, evidence-based recommendations to mitigate those risks.
Qualification & Experience
Masters or a Bachelor in Commerce/Accounting
CPA / CA Membership (or similar)
Minimum 10 - 15 years’ management experience in a Finance or Accounting environment
High level of discretion and sound judgement with managing confidential information
Willing to live and work in a remote location in PNG
Experience in using Attaché software or other similar Financial Management Information System
Proficient in Microsoft Office software; Word, PowerPoint, Outlook, Excel (advanced skills required).
Kiunga is a remote location in the North Fly District of Western Province of PNG. The candidate needs to be well suited to working in an isolated environment and must be self-motivated. He must be able to manage a FIFO roster of 8 weeks on/2 weeks off and have a well-balanced corporate profile with a strong finance element, and an ability to interact with rural communities as required.

[email protected]
.

Any demonstrated experience and results-based Monitoring & Evaluation Experience is highly preferable. 28267.description:
Stakeholder Relations and Policy Manager
VACANCY ANNOUNCEMENT
The Wildlife Conservation Society (WCS) is an international non-governmental organisation committed to working with communities, government, and other partners to manage wildlife and wild places for biodiversity and human well-being. WCS PNG is recruiting for a
Stakeholder Relations and Policy Manager
responsible for managing critical relationships with government (at national, provincial, district and local levels) and partner organisations, while working alongside WCS. The position is full-time and will be based in Port Moresby.
Main Responsibilities:
Serve as the primary point of contact with key government agencies integral to WCS’s marine and terrestrial biodiversity conservation objectives to conduct regular meetings, organise consultations, and undertake other activities to ensure government support and alignment with WCS activities, policy advice, and to ensure smooth project communications and coordination.
Provide strategic policy guidance and advice to the WCS programme, including leading or contributing to activities related to biodiversity and terrestrial and marine conservation policy development, policy coordination, and policy communications.
Provide technical support to WCS field staff and grantee partners on the development of inshore marine spatial plans aligned with PNG’s National Ocean Policy that will support the legal recognition or designation of priority areas as other effective area-based conservation measures (OECMs), locally managed marine areas (LMMAs), and other community-led marine conservation measures.
Support the NFA to advance marine spatial planning and legal designation processes for a large offshore marine protected area within PNG’s national Exclusive Economic Zone (EEZ) including the development of enforceable legal frameworks for priority offshore conservation areas. This will include support to the NFA to strengthen PNG’s national monitoring, control and surveillance (MCS) systems across both inshore and offshore marine areas.
In coordination with the Country Director and other managers, support strategic coordination with other CSO partner organisations, development partners, the private sector, and other relevant national stakeholders, including all activities implemented by WCS and external partners linked to the project.
Facilitate engagement with the Biodiversity and Climate Fund (BCF), in coordination with other WCS staff, to support its successful operationalisation and functioning as the country’s first conservation trust fund, as well as identify other opportunities for sustainable financing mechanisms for marine management at the national level.
Represent WCS PNG and its priorities and interests in meetings, conferences, and workshops, both within PNG and overseas where required.
Additionally, as WCS PNG is a flexible organisation, staff members are expected to undertake any other tasks that are allocated to them but which are not part of their regular job description.
Key Selection Criteria:
Bachelor’s degree in a relevant field, including though not limited to environmental management, constitutional or statutory law, or maritime law and policy.
At least five years of experience working with government and marine or terrestrial management organisations in PNG.
Demonstrated experience in ensuring close coordination with government agencies, particularly CEPA, at the national level.
Strong understanding of PNG government policies and governance systems, especially marine management laws and policies.
Demonstrated experience in supporting national level ocean planning and policy processes, with a preference for experience and expertise in the processes to establish offshore protections and enforcement processes.
Demonstrated experience in problem solving that incorporates kastom and adherence to institutional and donor policies.
Strong networks and relationships with stakeholders from government (at multiple levels), civil society and the private sector.
Ability to work sensitively and effectively with people of diverse cultures, value systems, perspectives and levels of education, and to manage and work with staff in these contexts.
Good communication and presentation skills; ability to persuasively convey the mission of WCS to diverse groups, especially to government, local stakeholders and constituents who are critical to the organisation’s overall prosperity.
A genuine interest in environmental management and the nature and societies of PNG.
Excellent interpersonal, written and oral communication skills.
Professional proficiency in oral and written English and Tok Pisin.
Experience with monitoring and evaluation and safeguards management is preferred.
Willingness to travel within PNG.
Application Process:
Please send an up-to-date Curriculum Vitae and letter of interest addressing the Key Selection Criteria to
[email protected]
with the subject line:
Application for Stakeholder Relations and Policy Manager
. Applications accepted until
5pm
,
Monday 7 September 2026
. Only short-listed candidates will be contacted for interviews.
WCS is an equal opportunity employer, and the organisation complies with all employment labor laws and regulations that prohibit discrimination in hiring, ensuring that candidates from all backgrounds are fairly and consistently considered during the recruitment process. We are dedicated to hiring and supporting a diverse workforce. We are committed to cultivating an inclusive work environment and look for future team members who share that same value. The organisation provides equal employment opportunities for all qualified candidates. The organisation does not discriminate for employment based on age, colour, disability, gender identify, national origin, race, religion, sexual orientation, veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by laws and regulations

ADVISOR– EMS
Reporting to the Senior Advisor, the Advisor - EMS provides environmental assurance to site operations through hazard identification, risk assessment, field verification, incident investigation, auditing and workforce engagement. The role supports operational teams to maintain compliance, implement effective controls and drive continual improvement in environmental performance.
The ideal candidate must have:
Tertiary qualification in Engineering or Science.
Current Class 3 PNG Driver's Licence
Demonstrated ability to identify environmental hazards, assess environmental risks and implement effective control measures.
Demonstrated experience conducting environmental incident investigations and root cause analysis using methodologies such as 5-Whys, ICAM or equivalent.
Demonstrated experience conducting environmental inspections, field interactions, planned task observations and compliance verification activities.
Demonstrated experience conducting internal audits, identifying non-conformances and verifying corrective actions.
Working knowledge of Environmental Management Systems and ISO 14001 requirements.
Strong data management, reporting and HSE management system experience.
Strong communication and influencing skills with the ability to engage operational personnel and contractors.
Job Responsibilities:
Identify environmental hazards and risks across operational areas.
Participate in environmental risk assessments and support the implementation of effective controls.
Conduct environmental interactions, inspections and planned task observations in operational work areas.
Conduct environmental incident investigations and support the timely close-out of corrective actions.
Conduct internal EMS audits, compliance inspections and verification activities.
Enter and maintain environmental data within the HSE Management System.
Respond to environmental incidents and provide field support during incident response activities.
Deliver environmental stewardship training, toolbox talks and awareness programs.
Support environmental reward and recognition programs.
Assist with the implementation and continual improvement of the Environmental Management System.

28261.description:
Newmont produces metals the world needs - safely, responsibly and with care for people, communities and the environment. With a 100+ year history, we continue to shape the future of mining through innovation and strong operational performance. By joining our inclusive, world-class team, you can help shape the future of mining and make a meaningful difference.
Our Lihir Operation, located on the beautiful island of Niolam, approximately 800km north of Papua New Guinea's capital, Port Moresby, is one of the world’s largest gold mines. Set within a geothermically active, extinct volcanic crater, Lihir operates an open-pit mine producing refractory ore, which undergoes pressure oxidation and conventional leaching to recover gold. Our workforce includes both residential and commute rosters, creating a diverse and dynamic team. Lihir offers a range of recreational facilities, including a gym, sports club, restaurant, bar, swimming pool, tennis and squash courts, and a 9-hole golf course. For those who enjoy the outdoors, the Lihir fishing and boating clubs provide access to pristine waters and beaches, while our onsite deli and café serve fresh local and imported produce, barista-made coffee, and freshly baked goods.
We are proud to work closely with the local Lihirian community and value its vibrant culture. Through initiatives like our School to Mine program, we offer meaningful employment, training, and development opportunities for Lihirian men and women, as well as scholarships and vocational apprenticeships. We also partner with the New Ireland Province to ensure economic benefits flow directly to the community, strengthening our commitment to sustainable development and positive local impact.
Your Impact
As Supervisor, Jaw Crushing, you will provide frontline leadership to ensure crushing operations are conducted safely, efficiently, and in line with operational standards while achieving production targets.
You will play a critical role in strengthening safety culture, building team capability, and driving continuous improvement across the operation.
Your leadership will influence workforce engagement, operational reliability, and the successful delivery of production outcomes, while helping embed Newmont's values and standards throughout the team.
As part of our team, you will
•    Lead and coordinate daily crushing activities to safely deliver production plans and operational targets.
•    Champion Newmont's safety culture through visible leadership, field interactions, workplace inspections, and proactive risk management.
•    Coach, mentor, and develop operators and permit personnel to build capability and strengthen team performance.
•    Drive continuous improvement initiatives that enhance operational efficiency, productivity, and team engagement.
•    Coordinate closely with maintenance, safety, control room, and operational teams to optimise plant performance.
•    Manage workforce deployment, shift coverage, and effective communication between crews.
•    Ensure compliance with operational procedures, permit-to-work requirements, and regulatory obligations.
•    Participate in incident investigations and support the implementation of corrective actions and learning opportunities.
•    Foster a positive, accountable culture where people are empowered to speak up, contribute ideas, and stop unsafe work.
Prerequisites for your success in this role
We're looking for a leader who combines strong operational experience with a genuine commitment to safety and people development
You will bring:
Minimum 5 years' experience in crushing, mineral processing, milling, or a similar mining environment.
At least 2 years of experience in a supervisory or frontline leadership position.
Demonstrated experience leading teams in a high-risk operational environment.
A strong safety mindset and proven ability to influence positive safety behaviours.
Experience coordinating operational activities and managing competing priorities.
Strong communication, coaching, and stakeholder engagement skills.
Experience using operational systems and software such as SAP and Microsoft Office applications.
The ability to build credibility through visibility, accountability, and leading by example.
Experience within large-scale mining or processing operations will be highly regarded.
Your work environment
This role is offered on a 28:14 Fly-in, Fly-out (FIFO) roster to Lihir Island, Papua New Guinea.
Our FIFO employees stay in a secure and comfortable camp environment, with ensuite, air-conditioned accommodation equipped with a mini fridge, television and Wi-Fi. A variety of nutritious meal options are available through the on-site catering facilities, while recreational and social amenities provide opportunities to relax and connect with colleagues while on roster.
You'll work closely with Operations, Maintenance, Safety, Support Services, and Control Room teams while leading a diverse workforce focused on safe and reliable plant performance. This role offers opportunities to broaden your operational knowledge, gain exposure to permit and isolation processes, and develop skills that can support future progression into broader leadership and advisory opportunities.
Why join Newmont
Lihir is one of the world's largest producing gold mines and one of Newmont's most significant operations.
Working at Lihir means joining a high-performing team committed to safety, operational excellence and delivering sustainable value for our people, communities and business.
Eligible employees may benefit from:
Competitive salary and annual performance incentive opportunities.
Company-funded FIFO travel and modern camp accommodation.
Access to health, wellbeing and employee assistance programs.
Ongoing learning, technical development and leadership training opportunities.
Exposure to large-scale mining operations and industry-leading technologies.
Career opportunities across Newmont's Australian, Papua New Guinean and global operations.
Access to a diverse range of on-site recreational, dining and wellbeing facilities.
The opportunity to be part of a workplace where safety, inclusion and growth are at the centre of everything we do.
Submit your application through our website quoting reference number 44396 before the advertised closing date: 7 September 2026.
At Newmont, our people are our strength and we’re committed to a safe, inclusive and supportive workplace. If you’re passionate about doing work that matters, join Newmont and help shape the future of mining.​
Learn more about our purpose and values:
About Newmont
​
Hear from our people:
Life at Newmont

With over 190 years of maritime experience, Svitzer is a global leader in towage and marine services. Across Australia and Papua New Guinea, our tug crews help keep ports safe, efficient, and moving. Workshop Operations Admin Coordinator
SPECTRA POM IS HIRING!
Spectra Industrial Limited - a Leader in Sales, Service and Hire of Forklifts, Gensets and Industrial Supplies, is seeking an organized and well experienced individual to join our POM Branch Workshop team, reporting to the Operations Manager.
Position Description
Position Title: Workshop Operations Admin Coordinator
Company: Spectra Industrial
Location: Port Moresby, Papua New Guinea
Reports To: Operations Manager / Branch Manager
Position Purpose
The Workshop Operations Admin Coordinator is responsible for supporting the effective administration and coordination of workshop operations, including customer service, client reporting, quotations, invoicing, work-in-progress reporting, staff coordination, and timely communication across teams. The role requires strong organization, accuracy, customer focus, and the ability to meet prompt deadlines in a busy workshop environment.
Key Responsibilities
Customer Service & Client Reporting
Provide professional and responsive service to external workshop customers.
Prepare and distribute weekly reports for external clients.
Ensure customer enquiries and requests are followed up accurately and on time.
Quotations, Invoicing & Accounts Support
Prepare quotations and invoicing for External Service, Engineering, Hydraulics and Machining jobs.
Support accurate billing, job documentation, and revenue capture.
Assist the Accounts Receivable team with external debt collection follow-ups.
Work in Progress Reporting
Prepare monthly reports for Management, including WIP (Work in Progress) updates.
Monitor job progress and maintain accurate workshop records.
Follow up outstanding job information to support timely reporting.
Workshop Staff
Coordination
Coordinate staff allocation and communication for both external and internal workshop jobs.
Liaise with workshop, operations, accounts, and customer service teams.
Support the smooth coordination of workshop activities to meet deadlines.
Workshop Operations Administration
Coordinate workshop operations professionally and efficiently.
Maintain accurate documentation, job files, and internal records.
Prioritize tasks under pressure and ensure prompt deadline management.
Key Competencies & Skills
Excellent interpersonal, written communication, customer care and negotiation skills.
Strong organizational ability with attention to detail and accuracy.
Ability to multitask, prioritize work and manage time efficiently.
Able to work under pressure, meet deadlines and coordinate across teams.
Customer-focused, proactive and well-motivated.
Qualifications & Experience
Year 12 education or higher educational background.
Broad knowledge of workshop operations and scheduling.
Solid knowledge and understanding of workshop service policies, procedures and systems.
Proficient computer skills, including Microsoft Office Suite: Word, PowerPoint, Outlook and Excel.
Minimum two years’ previous experience as a Workshop Service Coordinator, Fleet Coordinator, Workshop Administrator or related position.

About the role
Joining our sites services Maintenance team, you will install scaffolding and Safety Static lines on site as per Work Request, you will maintain impeccable safety standards and work as apart of a wider collaborative team.
Key Accountabilities
Key accountabilities of this position include.
Install scaffolding and Safety Static lines on site as per Work Request.
Assess the work, prepare JSEA and Permit as per required for the area of work.
Organise the materials required, assist to load and unload at work area.
Set up base plates on the ground at regular intervals (stop the upright poles slipping)
Install scaffolding poles (standards) & attaching the horizontal tubes (ledgers) to them with couples.
Fixing the scaffolding to the building or structure to make it more stable, using “short tie” tubes
Laying planks (battens) across the scaffolding for the workers to walk on.
Along with building and breaking down scaffolds, scaffold builders also install ladders, walkways and handrails at a construction site or shipping area using a variety of power tools and lifts.
Responsible for cleaning and preparing construction sites, including removing debris and dangerous materials.
Unload the scaffolding materials from a truck. These materials typically include the rails, planks, and ladders for the scaffold.
Check all materials and start creating scaffolds.
About You
To be considered for this role, it is essential that you
Hold a Grade 10 education or above.
Must hold a minimum of a Basic Scaffolder Certificate, Intermediate and Advanced desirable
Scaffold builders must be organized and able to follow instructions carefully.
Must be physically fit and have good manual dexterity to load and unload heavy materials on trucks and operate different machinery.
In addition, scaffold builders should be detail-oriented in order to spot potentially dangerous conditions, such as nearby power lines.
Must have good math skills for calculating measurements when building scaffolds.

28239.description:
Job Type:
Permanent
About us
K92 Mining Limited are the owners the high-grade Kainantu Gold Mine in Eastern Highlands Province. Since commencing operations in 2016, we have delivered consistent production growth. More importantly, we have contributed significantly to the economy of Papua New Guinea, more than 90% of our employees and contractors are from PNG and our local education and skills development initiatives which include scholarships, traineeships and adult literacy programs continue to bring significant benefit the communities in which we operate.
We are now transforming the operation with a new 1.2 mtpa process plant as well as extensive construction and expansion across site that will see us triple the output from our mine by 2027. In addition to our ongoing production success, we have an extensive exploration programme across our highly prospective tenement, making K92 a great place to build a long-term career.
About the role
Processing Services Operators are multi skilled technicians responsible for the day-to-day operation of the
•              mobile crushing and screening plant, conveying and stacking system.
•              concrete batching plant and agitator trucks
•              pastefill binder preparation plant
The Processing Services division operates on a continuous shift roster operating on both day and night shift.
Key / Major Accountabilities
Key accountabilities of this position include.
Perform the day-to-day operation of the mobile crushing and screening plant, conveying and stacking system; concrete batching plant and surface agitator trucks and pastefill binder preparation plant
Effectively operate and maintain mobile equipment including Light Vehicle, Front End Loader, Excavator, telehandler and forklift according to all K92 Operation & Maintenance procedures and fault reporting systems
Operate fixed plant equipment including jaw and cone crushers, screening plant, concrete batching plant, binder preparation plant, and cement offloading facility according to all K92 Operation & Maintenance procedures and fault reporting systems.
Monitor equipment and systems to ensure correct and safe operation.
Ensure quality of material being crushed, batched and prepared meets the correct quality standards by taking regular samples
Perform minor maintenance activities on all equipment and provide input and assistance maintenance personnel as needed.
Perform clean-up and housekeeping to ensure a safe, clean and productive work area.
Conduct machinery inspections throughout to ensure all systems are functioning properly.
Perform daily safety prestart maintenance checks.
Ensure all K92 safety standards, policies & procedures are always adhered to
Ensure that adequate duty of care is exercised in all aspects of work activities.
Ensure utmost compliance of Occupational Health and Safety Regulations and any site-specific rules which may apply within varying site operation.
About You
To be considered for this role, you must have a Grade 10 Certificate or technical trade Loader and excavator licences and relevant experience as well as Valid PNG Class 3 and Class 6 licence. In addition to this you will have some or all the following.
Five (5) or more years relevant work experience
Experience with operation and maintenance of mobile crushing equipment including but not limited to jaw crushers, cone crushers, screens, conveyors and stackers
Experience with concrete batching plant operations.
High risk work certificates including, Working at Heights, Confined Space Entry, Equipment Isolation
Ability to perform duties with minimum supervision.
Ability to work shift work
Able to communicate effectively at all levels, with good written communication skills.
Self-motivated with the ability to work under pressure and autonomously.
Excellent attention to detail and time management skills.
Strong active listening & interpersonal skills for rapport building, conflict resolution & training.
Life at K92
Our core values — Collaboration, Accountability, Respect, Excellence, and Safety — are central to our operations and fundamental to our success. K92 upholds a commitment to equal opportunity, striving to ensure that every individual can reach their highest potential without experiencing discrimination.
Our camp is well managed and provides residents with good, healthy meals made from locally sourced fresh produce as well as internet, cable tv and a gymnasium.
We believe in sharing our success with our employees. In addition to competitive salaries, we offer participation in long- and short-term incentive plans. We also offer savings programs, medical assistance, as well as access to our Wellbeing and employee assistance programs whilst working a friendly roster.
If you share our values and are looking for your next career step, come join us on this exciting journey. Submit your application through our website today.

Reporting directly to the
Manager – Human Resources,

Team Leadership & Culture:

28225.description:
POSITION TITLE:
CANCER INITIATIVE COORDINATOR SUPPORT– LAE
CONTEXT:
Médecins Sans Frontières (Doctors Without Borders) is a private, non-profit international humanitarian organization, founded in 1971 and working in 70 countries around the world. MSF provides medical assistance to populations in crisis, regardless of race, religion, belief, or political affiliation. In PNG, MSF has been working since 2007 in Lae, Tari, Bougainville, Gulf Province, and NCD Province. MSF is now working to support the Department of Health to improve access to care for patients in Lae, Jiwaka, and Highlands.
MAIN PURPOSE OF THE POSITION:
To support the Cancer Initiative Coordinator (CIC) in the coordination, analysis, and management of the Morobe Cancer Initiative's institutional relationships at provincial and national level. The position sustains continuous observation of the institutional environment across ANGAU, MoPHA, NDoH, and partner organizations, produces structured analysis to inform strategic and operational decisions, and supports the CIC in the day-to-day design and delivery of project activities with the Technical Working Group, Sub-Working Groups, and counterpart institutions, according to MSF protocols, standards and procedures in order to ensure the smooth running of the project.
RESPONSIBILITIES:
About the Morobe Cancer Initiative
The Morobe Cancer Initiative is a partnership between Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF), the Morobe Provincial Health Authority, and Papua New Guinea's National Department of Health. Based at ANGAU Memorial Hospital in Lae, the initiative supports the development of cancer care services across Morobe Province through the full continuum of prevention, screening, diagnosis, treatment, palliative care, pediatric oncology, and data. The initiative is governed by a Technical Working Group of Papua New Guinean clinicians and health authority representatives, organized into seven Sub-Working Groups. MSF supports the initiative through strategic coordination across all pillars and direct implementation of the palliative care component.
About the Role
The Cancer Initiative Coordinator Support works alongside the Cancer Initiative Coordinator (CIC) to sustain the institutional, relational, and analytical foundations of the initiative. The role combines ongoing observation and analysis of the institutional environment across ANGAU, MoPHA, and NDoH with operational support to the CIC in the day-to-day coordination of project activities. The position is based in Lae with periodic travel to Port Moresby. It is a national staff position for a duration of 6 months.
Accountabilities
Institutional Mapping and Analysis
Produce and maintain a living institutional map of counterpart actors, alliances, and decision pathways across ANGAU, MoPHA, and NDoH. Review quarterly with the Cancer Initiative Coordinator (CIC).
Maintain a standing institutional analysis document covering formal and informal dynamics, motivational and incentive structures, and patterns of engagement, including the distinction between genuine institutional commitment and performative compliance. Update quarterly.
Produce biweekly written context updates for the CIC, covering shifts in key actors, meetings observed, and emerging institutional signals.
Counterpart Relations and Coordination
Maintain field contacts and the project's counterpart relations database. Update after each significant interaction.
Prepare background materials and briefings in advance of TWG meetings, partner visits, and national-level missions.
Draft correspondence with counterparts and organize advocacy appointments at the request of the CIC.
Support the CIC in the ongoing design and implementation of MCI activities with the TWG, Sub-Working Groups, and counterpart institutions. Co-organize and co-facilitate workshops, strategic planning sessions, and partner engagement events as required.
Perform assigned additional responsibilities or tasks as required by the Project Coordinator
Meetings and Observation
Attend TWG Executive Committee, General Assembly, Sub-Working Group, MCI project, and key partner and counterpart meetings, in observer mode, as CIC team members, or as CIC representative when delegated.
Document observations and submit summary notes to the CIC after each meeting attended.
Communication, Translation, and Knowledge Continuity
Translate and interpret between English, Tok Pisin, and where required Hiri Motu, for project documents and meetings as required.
Prepare and deliver a contextual briefing to each incoming MSF staff member within two weeks of arrival, covering counterpart dynamics, communication norms, and the current institutional environment.
Produce an end of mission report on the status of MCI institutional relationships at provincial and national level.
SKILLS AND REQUIREMENTS:
Education
•        University degree Level in the field of Social Sciences required (Anthropology, Sociology, Polit-ical Science, Psychology, Public Administration, Public Policy, Development Studies, Interna-tional Relations, or related fields)
Experience
•          Essential: Demonstrated experience working in or alongside Papua New Guinean public institutions, NGOs, or research organizations.
•          Essential: Demonstrated capacity to produce structured written analysis in English.
•          Essential: Experience in data collection, observation, and reporting.
•          Desirable: Previous experience or academic background in health sector institutions, health system strengthening, or medical anthropology / sociology of health.
•          Desirable: Previous experience with international organizations or research projects.
•          Desirable: No current direct counterpart affiliation with ANGAU Memorial Hospital, the Morobe Provincial Health Authority, or the National Department of Health.
Languages
•          English essential, high-level command oral and written, including the production of analytical written reports.
•          Tok Pisin essential, high-level command oral and written.
•        Hiri Motu desirable
Knowledge
•           Essential: In-depth knowledge of Papua New Guinean institutional culture, governance structures, and public sector functioning.
•          Essential: Understanding of formal and informal authority structures in Papua New Guinea.
•          Essential: Computer literacy (word processing, spreadsheets, internet, email).
•        Desirable: Familiarity with the health sector, health system strengthening approaches, or the anthropology and sociology of health institutions.
Competencies
•          Results and Quality Orientation
•          Teamwork and Cooperation
•          Behavioral Flexibility
•          Commitment to MSF Principles
•          Stress Management
WORKING CONDITIONS
Fixed-term Contract
Based in Morobe
Candidates must be flexible with working hours and location
APPLICATION PROCESS
The applicants have to send their cover letter with an updated CV and a copy of any other relevant documents (diploma/degree/secondary school and training certificates, previous work certificates/recommendations) to:
By hand delivery:
Cassowary Road, Lae_Morobe province

Please clearly indicate in your application the position title and your phone number.  No document will be returned.
Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted

for the written tests and interviews. Written tests and interviews will be held in Morobe since recruitment for this position is for Morobe.
Medecins Sans Frontieres (MSF) is an equal-opportunity employer and encourages diversity, equity and Inclusion. Females and persons who are differently abled are encouraged to apply.
MSF doesn’t charge any application/recruitment fee. Nobody has the right to ask you for money, services, sexual favors or gifts in exchange for job. If you are victim or witness of similar situations, you may send us an email to

MSF is focused on ensuring that only those who share and demonstrate our values are recruited to work with us. To ensure we meet these standards, MSF has a “zero-tolerance” to any kind of abuse, exploitation, harassment and inappropriate behaviours.
MSF is committed to safeguarding, protection and fulfilling duty of care to patients, all people and communities we serve, and our staff. All staffs are required to share this commitment through signing and complying with our Behavioural Commitments and all relevant safeguarding policies.
Furthermore, receiving MSF job offers will be subject to satisfactory professional reference checks and clean criminal clearance.

28223.description:
Newmont produces metals the world needs - safely, responsibly and with care for people, communities and the environment. With a 100+ year history, we continue to shape the future of mining through innovation and strong operational performance. By joining our inclusive, world-class team, you can help shape the future of mining and make a meaningful difference.
Our Lihir Operation, located on the beautiful island of Niolam, approximately 800km north of Papua New Guinea's capital, Port Moresby, is one of the world’s largest gold mines. Set within a geothermically active, extinct volcanic crater, Lihir operates an open-pit mine producing refractory ore, which undergoes pressure oxidation and conventional leaching to recover gold. Our workforce includes both residential and commute rosters, creating a diverse and dynamic team. Lihir offers a range of recreational facilities, including a gym, sports club, restaurant, bar, swimming pool, tennis and squash courts, and a 9-hole golf course. For those who enjoy the outdoors, the Lihir fishing and boating clubs provide access to pristine waters and beaches, while our onsite deli and café serve fresh local and imported produce, barista-made coffee, and freshly baked goods.
We are proud to work closely with the local Lihirian community and value its vibrant culture. Through initiatives like our School to Mine program, we offer meaningful employment, training, and development opportunities for Lihirian men and women, as well as scholarships and vocational apprenticeships. We also partner with the New Ireland Province to ensure economic benefits flow directly to the community, strengthening our commitment to sustainable development and positive local impact.
Your Impact
As the Principal, Lihir International School, you'll provide strategic and operational leadership across both School to Mine and Lihir International School, ensuring the delivery of high-quality learning outcomes and a safe, inclusive environment for students and staff. You will play a key role in shaping educational programs, leading school operations, and fostering strong partnerships with parents, community stakeholders and Newmont to support student success and future pathways.
As Part of Our Team, You Will
Lead the day-to-day operations, strategic direction and overall performance of Lihir International School and the School to Mine Campus.
Provide leadership, coaching and performance management to teaching and non-teaching staff, fostering a positive, inclusive and high-performing culture.
Oversee curriculum development, implementation and continuous improvement to deliver high-quality educational outcomes and successful student pathways.
Manage school budgets, facilities, contractors, technology resources and administrative functions to ensure effective and sustainable operations.
Build strong relationships with students, parents, the School Council, community stakeholders and local schools to support student wellbeing and educational success.
Organise and lead school and community events and meetings, including School Council meetings, special school events, awards evenings, graduations, cultural celebrations, school productions and assemblies.
Manage health, safety and environmental risks across the School to Mine Campus and Lihir International School, including risk identification, mitigation planning, incident investigation and reporting.
Communicate effectively through school newsletters and engagement activities, working closely with parent groups and supporting community initiatives.
Support local community schools through partnership activities, mentoring opportunities and the development of local teachers and school leaders.
Promote responsible stewardship of school resources while supporting fundraising initiatives and community use of school facilities.
Prerequisites for Success in This Role
Bachelor’s degree in Education with current teacher registration.
Substantial Experience in school leadership, administration or a comparable educational leadership role.
Strong knowledge of Australian and PNG Curriculum, learning methodologies and educational best practices.
Demonstrated leadership capability with experience managing teams, building inclusive cultures and driving positive educational outcomes.
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to interpret data, make informed decisions and continuously improve student programs and outcomes.
Exceptional communication, stakeholder engagement and interpersonal skills, with the ability to build effective relationships with students, parents, staff, School Councils and community stakeholders.
High level of computer literacy, including proficiency in the Microsoft Office Suite and the ability to leverage technology to support educational and operational outcomes.
Strong organisational skills and the ability to manage competing priorities while maintaining a commitment to health, safety and educational excellence.
Your Work Environment
Reporting to the Director of People, Lihir HR, you will lead a team across the School to Mine Campus and Lihir International School. You will work closely with teaching and non-teaching staff, students, parents, the LIS School Council, Newmont leaders, Education Queensland International (EQI), the Department of Education International (DEi), local schools and community stakeholders to support educational excellence and student outcomes.
This role is offered on a 2-year fixed-term, full-time basis and operates on a residential 5:2 roster, working 10-hour days, based in Newmont’s Lihir townsite community, a gated precinct based on the coastline cliff with magnificent ocean views.
The townsite has Company provided housing (inc. utilities), international school (up to and including Year 10) and a range of recreational facilities including gym, sports club with restaurant, bar, swimming pool, tennis and squash courts and playground areas for the kids. There is also a 9-hole golf course on the island! Healthcare services are provided at the Lihir Medical Clinic.
An onsite deli and café provide access to fresh local and imported produce including grocery items, as well as barista-made coffees and freshly baked cakes. The company offers regular shipment of groceries and care packages for townsite residents to access goods not available on the island.
The Lihir fishing and boating clubs offer the opportunity to get out and enjoy the pristine waters and beaches around the island on the weekends.
A generous relocation package is provided to ensure smooth integration for you (and your family) to settle into island life.  You will also be eligible for medical insurance cover, annual flights home and schooling for eligible dependents. Newmont employees are rewarded with a competitive salary package and bonus scheme.
Why Join Newmont
Lihir is one of the world's largest producing gold mines and one of Newmont's most significant operations.
Working at Lihir means joining a high-performing team committed to safety, operational excellence and delivering sustainable value for our people, communities and business.
Eligible employees may benefit from:
Competitive salary and annual performance incentive opportunities.
Access to health, wellbeing and employee assistance programs.
Ongoing learning, technical development and leadership training opportunities.
Exposure to large-scale mining operations and industry-leading technologies.
Career opportunities across Newmont's Australian, Papua New Guinean and global operations.
The opportunity to be part of a workplace where safety, inclusion and growth are at the centre of everything we do.
At Newmont, our people are our strength and we’re committed to a safe, inclusive and supportive workplace. If you’re passionate about doing work that matters, join Newmont and help shape the future of mining.​
Learn more about our purpose and values:
About Newmont
​

Life at Newmont

Islands Petroleum is an independently owned fuel and lubes distributor, and the exclusive distributor for Mobil Lubricants in Papua New Guinea. Islands Petroleum operates bulk fuel and lubricant Depots and Distribution Centres in the Islands, Momase, Southern, and the Highlands regions.
We are currently seeking a seasoned professional for a Talent Acquisition Coordinator to join our Human Resource Team, to be based at our Port Moresby office.
The Role & Responsibilities
Reporting to the Manager – HR and Talent,
y
ou will coordinate recruitment activities across our operational and corporate workforce, with a strong focus on recruiting both operational and technical / supervisory employees. You will manage the recruitment process from vacancy through to commencement, ensuring candidates have a positive experience while vacancies are filled efficiently and in line with our workforce requirements.

Develop and execute sustainable recruitment strategy based on company’s workforce needs & objectives
Coordinate end-to-end recruitment campaigns across the business.
Manage high-volume recruitment of operational employees.
Advertise vacancies across appropriate job boards, social media and recruitment channels.
Screen applications and conduct telephone/video pre-screening.
Coordinate interviews, assessments and pre-employment requirements.
Maintain accurate recruitment records and ensure candidates progress efficiently through the recruitment process.
Liaise closely with Depot Managers, Operations Leaders and hiring managers to understand workforce requirements.
Coordinate medicals, police checks, licence verification and other role-specific pre-employment checks.
Support the onboarding process and ensure new employees are ready to commence safely and effectively.
Develop and maintain talent pools for ongoing driver and operational recruitment needs.

Demonstrated experience in recruitment coordination, talent acquisition or a similar role
Experience with high-volume recruitment
Excellent organisational and time-management skills.
Strong communication and stakeholder-management skills.
The ability to manage multiple vacancies and competing priorities.
Strong attention to detail and a commitment to compliance.
Experience using applicant tracking systems and recruitment platforms.
A professional, approachable and candidate-focused manner.
The confidence to work closely with operational leaders and challenge or influence when required.
Excellent analytical mind with strong verbal and written communication skills
Benefits:
A supportive and collaborative People & Culture team.
A dynamic and varied recruitment environment.
The opportunity to make a real impact on workforce capability.
Career development and learning opportunities.
A strong focus on safety, inclusion, teamwork, excellence and employee experience.

28219.description:
Newmont produces metals the world needs - safely, responsibly and with care for people, communities and the environment. With a 100+ year history, we continue to shape the future of mining through innovation and strong operational performance. By joining our inclusive, world-class team, you can help shape the future of mining and make a meaningful difference.
Our Lihir Operation, located on the beautiful island of Niolam, approximately 800km north of Papua New Guinea's capital, Port Moresby, is one of the world’s largest gold mines. Set within a geothermically active, extinct volcanic crater, Lihir operates an open-pit mine producing refractory ore, which undergoes pressure oxidation and conventional leaching to recover gold. Our workforce includes both residential and commute rosters, creating a diverse and dynamic team. Lihir offers a range of recreational facilities, including a gym, sports club, restaurant, bar, swimming pool, tennis and squash courts, and a 9-hole golf course. For those who enjoy the outdoors, the Lihir fishing and boating clubs provide access to pristine waters and beaches, while our onsite deli and café serve fresh local and imported produce, barista-made coffee, and freshly baked goods.
We are proud to work closely with the local Lihirian community and value its vibrant culture. Through initiatives like our School to Mine program, we offer meaningful employment, training, and development opportunities for Lihirian men and women, as well as scholarships and vocational apprenticeships. We also partner with the New Ireland Province to ensure economic benefits flow directly to the community, strengthening our commitment to sustainable development and positive local impact.
Your impact
As our High School English Teacher, you will play a pivotal role in shaping the educational journey of students in Years 7-10, with potential opportunities to teach senior secondary students in the future. You'll foster a safe, inclusive and engaging learning environment where students are challenged to think critically, communicate confidently and reach their full potential.
Your contribution will extend beyond the classroom as you help students develop the skills, confidence and knowledge needed to succeed both academically and personally.
As part of our team you will
•    Deliver engaging English lessons aligned to the Australian Curriculum and PNG Standards Based Curriculum.
•    Create safe, inclusive and supportive learning environments that promote student wellbeing and achievement.
•    Develop lesson plans, learning resources and assessment activities that inspire curiosity and learning.
•    Monitor, assess and report on student progress while partnering with parents and the school community to support learning outcomes.
•    Contribute to co-curricular and extra-curricular programs that enrich the student experience.
•    Collaborate with teaching colleagues, school leadership and support staff to continuously improve educational outcomes.
•    Uphold the values, safety standards and expectations of both Lihir International School and Newmont.
Prerequisites for your success in this role
You are a dedicated educator with a passion for English and a commitment to helping students succeed.
To be successful, you will possess:
A bachelor’s degree in education and current teacher registration.
A minimum of five years' relevant teaching experience.
Demonstrated experience teaching English in a secondary school environment.
Strong knowledge of the Australian Curriculum and the PNG Standards Based Curriculum, particularly across Years 7-10.
Understanding of PNG national examinations for Grades 8 and 10.
The ability to differentiate learning and support students with diverse learning needs.
Excellent communication, relationship-building and interpersonal skills.
Strong digital literacy and proficiency with contemporary educational technologies and Microsoft Office applications.
A willingness to contribute to the broader life of the school through extra-curricular activities and community engagement.
Your work environment
Lihir International School is a dynamic and diverse educational community committed to delivering high-quality learning outcomes for students and families in Papua New Guinea. As part of a collaborative team of education professionals, you'll work closely with students, parents, colleagues and the wider Newmont community to provide an exceptional educational experience.
This role offers the opportunity to live and work in a unique island environment while experiencing a strong sense of community and cultural diversity. As a residential position, company-provided housing and a competitive remuneration package are available to support your lifestyle.
Working Conditions
This role is offered on a residential 5:2 roster, based in Newmont’s Lihir townsite community, a gated precinct based on the coastline cliff with magnificent ocean views.
The townsite has Company provided housing (inc. utilities), international school (up to and including Year 10) and a range of recreational facilities including gym, sports club with restaurant, bar, swimming pool, tennis and squash courts and playground areas for the kids. There is also a 9-hole golf course on the island! Healthcare services are provided at the Lihir Medical Clinic.
An onsite deli and café provide access to fresh local and imported produce including grocery items, as well as barista-made coffees and freshly baked cakes. The company offers regular shipment of groceries and care packages for townsite residents to access goods not available on the island.
The Lihir fishing and boating clubs offer the opportunity to get out and enjoy the pristine waters and beaches around the island on the weekends.
A generous relocation package is provided to ensure smooth integration for you (and your family) to settle into island life.  You will also be eligible for medical insurance cover, annual flights home and schooling for eligible dependants. Newmont employees are rewarded with a competitive salary package and bonus scheme.
Why join Newmont
We support our people with competitive rewards, quality accommodation, professional development opportunities and a culture that values collaboration, respect and continuous learning. As part of our team, your contribution will help shape the future of young learners while supporting one of the world's leading mining organizations.
Submit your application through our website quoting reference number 44323 before the advertised closing date: 3 September 2026.
At Newmont, our people are our strength and we’re committed to a safe, inclusive and supportive workplace. If you’re passionate about doing work that matters, join Newmont and help shape the future of mining.​
Learn more about our purpose and values:
About Newmont
​
Hear from our people:
Life at Newmont

28215.description:
DESIGN MANAGER
The practical, buildable, no-surprises kind.
Port Moresby | Full-time
Atlas is growing, and we’re looking for an experienced
Design Manager
to lead our design and drafting team across Steel Haus modular housing, structural steel and design-and-build construction projects.
This is not a role for someone who only understands design from behind a desk.
We need someone who understands how drawings translate into fabrication, construction and finished buildings — and who can make sure problems are resolved before they reach the workshop or site.
WHAT YOU’LL BE DOING
You’ll take ownership of the Atlas design function and lead projects from concept and tender design through to construction issue.
You’ll coordinate architectural, structural, civil and building-services design, making sure everything is buildable, compliant and properly coordinated.
You’ll work closely with our estimating and commercial teams to produce the drawings and design information needed to price and win work.
You’ll also work directly with our Steel Haus, fabrication and construction teams on shop drawings, detailing and practical solutions that can actually be built.
The role includes:
Leading and managing the design and drafting team.
Taking designs from concept through tender to IFC documentation.
Coordinating architectural, structural, civil and services design.
Reviewing drawings for buildability, clashes and constructability.
Managing drawing registers, revisions, standards and CAD/BIM systems.
Supporting estimating and tender submissions with drawings and design information.
Working with fabrication teams on structural steel and Steel Haus shop drawings.
Coordinating external engineers, consultants, surveyors and certifiers.
Managing design requirements for NCDC, NCD Building Board and other approving authorities.
Improving Atlas design standards, details, templates and systems.
WHO THIS SUITS
You’ll need solid building and construction design experience and the confidence to lead a team, make decisions and keep projects moving.
You should have:
A qualification in architecture, building design, architectural drafting, civil engineering, structural engineering or a related field.
At least
7 years’ experience
in building or construction design.
Previous experience leading a design or drafting team.
Advanced
AutoCAD
skills.
Strong knowledge of relevant
Australian Standards and AS/NZS requirements
.
Experience taking projects from concept through to construction documentation.
A strong understanding of detailing, constructability and value engineering.
The ability to manage several projects and deadlines at the same time.
Strong communication skills and the ability to work with clients, consultants, commercial teams, workshops and construction crews.
Experience with
Revit/BIM, modular construction, structural steel fabrication, design-and-build projects and PNG building approvals
will be highly regarded.
If your drawings look good but don’t work when they reach the workshop or site, this probably isn’t the role for you.
WHY YOU’LL LIKE WORKING HERE
At Atlas, the design team is close to the work.
We design it.
We fabricate it.
We build it.
That means you get to see your designs move from an idea on screen to something real.
You’ll have the opportunity to lead and improve the design function across a growing PNG business working in
steel, construction, housing and infrastructure
.
The expectation is simple:
Produce good designs. Make them buildable. Keep projects moving. Get the details right.
HOW TO APPLY
Send your CV and a short cover letter to:
[email protected]
Use
“Design Manager”
in the subject line.
Applications close
Thursday, 3 September 2026
.
Only shortlisted applicants will be contacted.
ATLAS
BUILT BY PAPUA NEW GUINEANS.

28214.description:
Job Type:
Permanent
About us
K92 Mining Limited are the owners the high-grade Kainantu Gold Mine in Eastern Highlands Province. Since commencing operations in 2016, we have delivered consistent production growth. More importantly, we have contributed significantly to the economy of Papua New Guinea, more than 90% of our employees and contractors are from PNG and our local education and skills development initiatives which include scholarships, traineeships and adult literacy programs continue to bring significant benefit the communities in which we operate.
We are now transforming the operation with a new 1.2 mtpa process plant as well as extensive construction and expansion across site that will see us triple the output from our mine by 2027. In addition to our ongoing production success, we have an extensive exploration programme across our highly prospective tenement, making K92 a great place to build a long-term career.
About the role
In this role you will report to the Superintendent - Processing and oversee process plant operations whist collaboratively working with the wider processing team to ensure the efficient, safe, and continuous operation of the Process Plant including the Mill and the Laboratory in achieving production targets. In addition, maintaining high work standards in accordance with government regulations and K92 Mining policy.
Key / Major Accountabilities
Key accountabilities of this position include.
Monitor, audit and optimize plant metallurgical performance.
Provide technical support, training and guidance to technical staff and operation crews.
Complete regular metallurgical accounting and reporting.
Ensuring the processing plant is operated to meet production targets.
Developing innovative solutions to both medium and long-term projects integral to the process plant.
Lead and report on studies relevant to production improvement, cost saving initiatives and project development.
Work in collaboration with Processing Manager or designate to ensure that the entire ore processing operation meets environmental regulations/standards.
Preparing process plant scope documents.
Assist the Processing Manager in cost budget preparation and forecasts.
Regular liaison with engineering and technical staff. This includes maintaining open dialogue and teamwork between Maintenance, Operations and Environmental departments.
Oversee weekly report and prepare and compile monthly reports to management team as required.
Review incidents and ensure learnings are communicated and implemented.
Perform all other tasks relating and as directed by the Process Manager.
Maintain safe work standards and practices in accordance with government and company policy
About You
To be considered for this role, it is essential you will have some or all the following.
A Bachelor’s Degree in Metallurgy, Mineral Processing or Chemical Engineering.
Minimum of (10) years’ experience working in a Mineral Processing Plant.
Sulphide Mineral Flotation experience, crushing and grinding experience.
Sound knowledge of Mining industry Safety, Environmental and Operational Practices in an underground mine.
Sound knowledge of Mill Control systems
Ability to diagnose fault with equipment and processes within the Operations area.
Able to lead, provide training and coaching to staff within the processing department.
Strong planning and analytical skills.
A team player with good computer skills.
Able to communicate effectively across all levels.
Class three (3) driver’s license.
Ability to train process plant personnel in all aspects of their trade – particularly in diagnosis and fault finding, quality control, thoroughness and record keeping.
Must be a self-starter, and very resourceful, with the ability to find solutions to problems to ensure the equipment availability is high.
Flexible, adaptable and be a team player.
Life at K92
Our core values — Collaboration, Accountability, Respect, Excellence, and Safety — are central to our operations and fundamental to our success. K92 upholds a commitment to equal opportunity, striving to ensure that every individual can reach their highest potential without experiencing discrimination.
Our camp is well managed and provides residents with good, healthy meals made from locally sourced fresh produce as well as internet, cable tv and a gymnasium.
We believe in sharing our success with our employees. In addition to competitive salaries, we offer participation in long- and short-term incentive plans. We also offer savings programs, medical assistance, as well as access to our Wellbeing and employee assistance programs whilst working a friendly roster.
If you share our values and are looking for your next career step, come join us on this exciting journey. Submit your application through our website today.
THIS POSITION IS OPEN ONLY TO CANDIDATES WHO HAVE THE RIGHT TO LIVE & WORK IN PNG WITHOUT SPONSORSHIP

28211.description:
Newmont produces metals the world needs - safely, responsibly and with care for people, communities and the environment. With a 100+ year history, we continue to shape the future of mining through innovation and strong operational performance. By joining our inclusive, world-class team, you can help shape the future of mining and make a meaningful difference.
Our Lihir Operation, located on the beautiful island of Niolam, approximately 800km north of Papua New Guinea's capital, Port Moresby, is one of the world’s largest gold mines. Set within a geothermically active, extinct volcanic crater, Lihir operates an open-pit mine producing refractory ore, which undergoes pressure oxidation and conventional leaching to recover gold. Our workforce includes both residential and commute rosters, creating a diverse and dynamic team. Lihir offers a range of recreational facilities, including a gym, sports club, restaurant, bar, swimming pool, tennis and squash courts, and a 9-hole golf course. For those who enjoy the outdoors, the Lihir fishing and boating clubs provide access to pristine waters and beaches, while our onsite deli and café serve fresh local and imported produce, barista-made coffee, and freshly baked goods.
We are proud to work closely with the local Lihirian community and value its vibrant culture. Through initiatives like our School to Mine program, we offer meaningful employment, training, and development opportunities for Lihirian men and women, as well as scholarships and vocational apprenticeships. We also partner with the New Ireland Province to ensure economic benefits flow directly to the community, strengthening our commitment to sustainable development and positive local impact.
Your impact
Join a world-class analytical laboratory supporting one of the world's leading gold mining operations. As an Laboratory Technician, you will play a vital role in delivering accurate, reliable laboratory results that support critical operational decisions across the business. Working within a safety-focused and quality-driven environment, you'll contribute to laboratory excellence through sample analysis, quality assurance activities, equipment management, and continuous improvement initiatives. Your expertise will help maintain compliance with ISO17025 standards while ensuring laboratory operations run efficiently and effectively.
As part of our team you will
Consistently uphold laboratory safety and compliance standards.[PL1.1]
Prepare, handle, and analyse samples using specialised laboratory equipment and established analytical procedures.
Support quality assurance and quality control (QA/QC) activities to maintain the integrity and accuracy of laboratory results.
Conduct daily pre-start inspections and support safe laboratory operations.
Perform weekly stocktakes and assist with the management of critical laboratory consumables.
Prepare reagents and standardise solutions to support analytical processes.
Profile laboratory jobs, manage worksheets and documentation, and maintain accurate records.
Collaborate with laboratory teams, operational stakeholders, and internal clients to deliver timely analytical results.
Support continuous improvement initiatives, including Lean 5S activities and workplace organisation programs.
Assist the Laboratory Supervisor with delegated responsibilities and act in a leading-hand capacity when required.
Contribute to daily KPI reporting, shift handovers, and operational communications.
Prerequisites for your success in this role
A Bachelor's degree in Chemistry, Analytical Chemistry, Applied Chemistry, or a related discipline.
A minimum of 4 years' experience in a laboratory role within a mining, minerals processing, or metallurgical environment.
Practical experience working with analytical equipment such as LECO and Atomic Absorption Spectrometry (AAS).
Working knowledge of ISO17025 laboratory quality standards and compliance requirements.
Experience in carrying out Fire Assay activities [PL2.1]related tasks.
Experience in QA/QC processes, sample preparation, reagent preparation, and laboratory documentation.
Strong attention to detail, organisational skills, and a commitment to accuracy.
Proficiency with Microsoft Office applications and laboratory data management systems, including CCLAS or equivalent systems.
The ability to work collaboratively within a diverse team while maintaining strong safety and operational standards.
Your work environment
Located at our Lihir operation, this role offers the opportunity to work within a highly specialised analytical laboratory supporting mining and processing activities unique to one of the world's premier gold operations. You'll collaborate with experienced laboratory professionals, technical specialists, operational teams, and internal stakeholders while gaining exposure to advanced analytical techniques and complex mineral analysis.
Working Conditions
This role is offered on a 28:14 Fly in, Fly out (FIFO) roster to Lihir Island, Papua New Guinea
Our FIFO employees stay in a secure and comfortable camp, in an en-suited and airconditioned room equipped with mini fridge, TV and Wi-Fi. A variety of healthy meal options are catered for at our mess; and the wet mess provides a relaxed social setting where employees can unwind with a game of pool or darts.
Why join Newmont
This is more than a laboratory role. It offers a genuine career pathway with opportunities to develop toward leadership positions, including progression into Laboratory Supervisor roles. In addition, employees have access to professional development opportunities, including support for Royal Australian Chemical Institute (RACI) membership and ongoing technical training.
Submit your application through our website quoting reference number 44332 before the advertised closing date: 2 September 2026.
At Newmont, our people are our strength and we’re committed to a safe, inclusive and supportive workplace. If you’re passionate about doing work that matters, join Newmont and help shape the future of mining.​
Learn more about our purpose and values:
About Newmont
​

Life at Newmont

Job Type:
Permanent
About us
K92 Mining Limited are the owners the high-grade Kainantu Gold Mine in Eastern Highlands Province. Since commencing operations in 2016, we have delivered consistent production growth. More importantly, we have contributed significantly to the economy of Papua New Guinea, more than 90% of our employees and contractors are from PNG and our local education and skills development initiatives which include scholarships, traineeships and adult literacy programs continue to bring significant benefit the communities in which we operate.
We are now transforming the operation with a new 1.2 mtpa process plant as well as extensive construction and expansion across site that will see us triple the output from our mine by 2027. In addition to our ongoing production success, we have an extensive exploration programme across our highly prospective tenement, making K92 a great place to build a long-term career.
About the role
Joining our underground mining team, you will operate the loading and unloading truck, while upholding the Company’s Code of Conduct, by display the appropriate work attitude and teamwork within the underground areas.
Key Accountabilities
Key accountabilities of this position include.
This position reports to the Shift Supervisor and forms part of the Mining team accountable for providing effective services underground.
Maintain good working relationship with colleague workers.
Strong commitment to safety
Responsible to operate LHD’s and low-profile trucks.
Responsible for house keeping
Responsible for cleaning after use and checking before use
About You
To be considered for this role, it is essential that you
Possess PNG Class 6 and 7 driver license
Has underground mining work experience.
Ability to read and write both Pidgin and English
